name: Vision Bank
legal_name: Vision Bank (Closed Joint Stock Company, CR 1010850478; formerly Saudi Digital Bank)
founded: Cabinet approval of the licence (as Saudi Digital Bank) announced by SAMA on 22 Jun 2021, capital SAR 1.5bn; pilot phase for a limited number of clients from 1 Jan 2025; SAMA non-objection to commence digital banking operations on 15 Sep 2025.
ownership_summary: Unlisted closed joint-stock company founded by a consortium of companies and individual investors led by Abdul Rahman bin Saad Al-Rashed and Sons (Artar); most founding shareholders are not named. The only named shareholder is Tadawul-listed Al Moammar Information Systems (MIS), which put in SAR 25m as a founding shareholder (2021) and signed for SAR 23.75m of a capital increase from SAR 1.5bn to SAR 3bn on 28 Jan 2026 at a SAR 3.2bn pre-money valuation. Percentages are not disclosed. The website footer still showed SAR 1.5bn capital on 12 Oct 2026.

shareholders.holder: Consortium led by Abdul Rahman bin Saad Al-Rashed and Sons Company (Artar); members and stakes not disclosed
Al Moammar Information Systems Co. (MIS, Tadawul-listed): SAR 25m founding contribution; SAR 23.75m subscription in the Jan 2026 capital increase; stake not disclosed

government_link: Not found after research: no government or sovereign shareholder is named in the sources found (private consortium). Licensed by Cabinet decision and supervised by SAMA. Checked 2026-10-12.
group_structure: Standalone bank; no parent or subsidiaries found. Shareholders are not named beyond the Al-Rashed-led consortium and MIS, so group links cannot be mapped. SAMA's digital-banks register still lists the bank under its former name, Saudi Digital Bank.
footprint: Saudi Arabia only; digital-only (iOS and Android app, Noura chat assistant, no branches found). National address 6537 Riyadh 12432-2693 (website footer). Checked 2026-10-12.
customer_segments: Individuals and families (current accounts, term deposits, goal savings, Family Banking with children's accounts); entrepreneurs and SMEs (medium and small businesses; business banking shown as 'Launching soon').
business_lines: Personal: current account, Family Banking (parent-controlled accounts and debit cards for children and teens with chores, rewards and gamified learning), Murabaha Term Deposit (7 days to 1 year, from SAR 1,000), Goal Based Savings, Noura AI conversational assistant for account opening, transfers and beneficiaries, a SAR 1,000,000 'Millionaire' prize campaign, payment cards, local transfers and bill payments. Business: SME banking page says 'Launching soon'. No investment, brokerage or fund product found (checked 2026-10-12).

capabilities.wealth_summary: Vision Bank is an early-stage retail and SME digital bank that describes itself as the first Islamic digital bank powered by AI (Noura, a conversational assistant for account opening, transfers and beneficiaries). Its savings and deposit offer is a Murabaha Term Deposit (7 days to 1 year, from SAR 1,000, up to 6% for a 1-year term, partial withdrawal of up to 20%) and Goal Based Savings (banner 'up to 5.5%'), plus Family Banking and a SAR 1,000,000 prize campaign. No investment, brokerage, fund, advisory or private-banking offer was found (checked 12 Oct 2026), and the SME proposition is still marked 'Launching soon'. SAMA cleared full operations on 15 Sep 2025 after a pilot from Jan 2025. The shareholders agreed to double capital to SAR 3bn in Jan 2026, and a 2026 partnership with Publicis Sapient is to design and run an innovation strategy and hub for new individual and SME propositions.

initiatives.what: Cabinet approved licences for two local digital banks: STC Bank and Saudi Digital Bank (SAR 1.5bn, group led by Abdul Rahman bin Saad Al-Rashed and Sons), announced by SAMA
Pilot phase launched for a limited number of clients after SAMA's go-ahead: Murabaha deposits, payment cards, domestic transfers and bill payments
SAMA granted non-objection to commence digital banking operations; Vision Bank became the third digital bank approved
Bank announced a second phase of expansion across customer segments, with Noura AI account opening and transfers and family savings; entrepreneur and SME accounts to follow soon
Capital increase from SAR 1.5bn to SAR 3bn agreed at a SAR 3.2bn pre-money valuation; MIS signed for SAR 23.75m
Sponsored feature positions the bank as the first AI-powered Islamic digital bank, with Family Banking and a planned SME offer
Strategic partnership with Publicis Sapient announced around Money20/20 Middle East, Riyadh (release undated)

opportunities: Product set is current accounts, Family Banking, Murabaha term deposits and goal savings; no investment product on the site, and the bank is only a year into full operations (S2-S4, S7).
Capital is being doubled to SAR 3bn (agreed 28 Jan 2026) and a Publicis Sapient innovation hub is set up to create new propositions for individuals and SMEs (S12, S16).
Family Banking and goal-based savings suggest a long-term saving and financial-education focus that could extend to investing (S4, S6, S15).
barriers: Early stage: pilot from Jan 2025, full operations cleared Sep 2025; no customer or balance-sheet figures published (S7, S13).
Shariah-governed bank: any shelf needs Shariah screening and committee approval (S1).
Stated near-term roadmap is SME banking and AI-led service (Noura), not wealth; no wealth, investments or digital-product head named (S5, S15, S16).
Innovation work is being scoped with Publicis Sapient, which may shape build-versus-partner choices (S16).

CEO: Abdul Shakeel Aidaroos is quoted as CEO (Okaz 1 Jan 2026; Zawya/Publicis Sapient release, 2026) but the website lists no management and his start date is not known.
